D: A grumpy teacher, a grieving cook and a troubled student are stuck at a New England boarding school over Christmas 1970.
P: Serve dessert when Mr Hunham orders the cherries jubilee.
S: Mary's grilled cheese and tomato soup
Creamy tomato soup with sourdough cheddar and mozzarella toasties

Golden grilled cheese of vintage cheddar and mozzarella on buttered sourdough, cut into fingers for dunking in a smoky tomato soup. Fry 1 diced onion and 2 garlic cloves in 2 tbsp olive oil for 5 minutes. Add 2 x 400g tins crushed tomatoes, 1 tsp smoked paprika, 1 tsp sugar and 300ml chicken stock and simmer 15 minutes, then blitz smooth and stir in 50ml cream. Butter 8 slices sourdough on the outside and fill with 150g cheddar and 100g mozzarella. Fry over medium heat for 3 minutes a side until golden. Cut into fingers.
Creamy clam chowder with bacon, potato and celery

Creamy New England clam chowder with smoky bacon, potato, thyme and fresh clams, served in mugs with oyster crackers. Fry 3 diced rashers bacon until crisp, add 1 onion and 2 celery sticks and cook 5 minutes. Stir in 2 tbsp plain flour, then 400ml fish stock, 300g diced potato and a few thyme sprigs and simmer 12 minutes. Add 1kg cleaned clams, cover and cook 4 minutes until open, then remove the shells. Stir in 300ml cream and heat through. Season with pepper and serve with oyster crackers.
M: Roast chicken with sage and lemon breadcrumb stuffing

Roast chicken with bread and herb stuffing, crunchy roast potatoes, glazed carrots and gravy, a small Christmas dinner done properly. Fry 1 diced onion in 40g butter, mix with 150g fresh breadcrumbs, 2 tbsp chopped sage, the zest of 1 lemon and 1 egg, and stuff a 1.8kg chicken. Rub with butter and salt and roast at 200C for 1 hour 20 minutes. Roast 1kg halved potatoes in oil for 50 minutes. Glaze 4 carrots with 20g butter and 1 tbsp honey. Rest the chicken, then make gravy from the juices with 1 tbsp flour and 350ml stock.
W: Cherries warmed with orange and brandy, flamed, over vanilla ice cream

Dark cherries simmered in a buttery orange and brandy sauce, flamed at the table and spooned hot over vanilla ice cream. Drain a 680g jar pitted cherries, keeping 150ml syrup. Melt 30g butter with 60g brown sugar in a wide pan, add the syrup and the zest and juice of 1 orange and simmer 3 minutes. Stir in 1 tsp cornflour mixed with water, then add the cherries and warm through. Off the heat, pour in 60ml brandy, then carefully light it with a long match and let the flames die down. Spoon over 1L vanilla ice cream.
K: Hot water, bourbon, honey, lemon and cinnamon with a clove lemon slice

Bourbon with hot water, honey, lemon and a cinnamon stick, a warming nightcap for a New England winter. Plain honey lemon for non-drinkers. Boil 800ml water. In each of 4 heatproof mugs, put 1 tbsp honey, the juice of half a lemon, 45ml bourbon and a cinnamon stick. Top each with 200ml hot water and stir until the honey dissolves. Stud a lemon slice with 3 cloves and float it on top. Leave out the bourbon for anyone not drinking.

dishes.n: Mary's grilled cheese and tomato soup
dishes.make_ahead: Make the soup up to 3 days ahead and reheat; fill and fry the sandwiches just before serving

steps.text: Fry the onion and garlic in the oil until soft.
Add the tomatoes, paprika, sugar and stock and simmer.
Blitz the soup smooth and stir in the cream.
Butter the outsides of the sourdough and fill with the cheddar and mozzarella.
Fry over medium heat until golden on both sides. Cut into fingers and serve with the soup.

veg.n: Mary's grilled cheese and tomato soup (vegetarian)
veg.make_ahead: Make the soup up to 3 days ahead and reheat gently; fill and fry the sandwiches just before serving

steps.text: Fry the onion and garlic in the oil until soft.
Add the tomatoes, paprika, sugar and stock and simmer.
Blitz the soup smooth and stir in the cream.
Butter the outsides of the sourdough and fill with the cheddar and mozzarella.
Fry over medium heat until golden on both sides. Cut into fingers and serve with the soup.

dishes.make_ahead: Simmer the base up to 1 day ahead, covered in the fridge; add the clams and cream when reheating so the clams stay tender

steps.text: Fry the bacon until crisp, add the onion and celery and cook until soft.
Stir in the flour, then the stock, potato and thyme and simmer.
Add the clams, cover and cook until open, then remove the empty shells.
Stir in the cream and heat through. Season with pepper and serve with oyster crackers.

veg.n: Boston trip mushroom and potato chowder
veg.make_ahead: Up to 2 days ahead, reheat gently; stir in the cream on the night

steps.text: Melt the butter and fry the mushrooms over high heat until golden.
Add the smoked paprika, onion and celery and cook until soft.
Stir in the flour, then the stock, kombu, potato and thyme and simmer until the potato is tender.
Lift out the kombu, stir in the cream and heat through. Season with salt and pepper and serve with the crackers.

dishes.make_ahead: Make the stuffing up to 1 day ahead, covered in the fridge; stuff and roast the chicken on the day

steps.text: Fry the onion in some of the butter, then mix with the breadcrumbs, sage, lemon zest and egg. Stuff the chicken.
Rub the chicken with butter and salt and roast at 200C.
Roast the potatoes in oil on another tray.
Glaze the carrots in butter and honey.
Rest the chicken, then make gravy from the juices with the flour and stock.

veg.n: Barton Academy Christmas stuffed roast pumpkin
veg.make_ahead: Make the stuffing up to 1 day ahead, covered in the fridge; halve, fill and roast the pumpkin on the day

steps.text: Fry the onion in some of the butter, then mix with the breadcrumbs, sage, lemon zest and egg.
Halve the pumpkins lengthways and scoop out the seeds. Rub with butter and salt and roast cut side down at 200C.
Turn the pumpkins over, pack the stuffing into the hollows and roast until golden. Roast the potatoes in oil on another tray.
Glaze the carrots in butter and honey.
Pour off the roasting juices, stir in the flour, whisk in the stock and simmer into gravy.

dishes.make_ahead: Make the cherry sauce up to 2 days ahead and keep it chilled; reheat and add the brandy on the night

steps.text: Drain the cherries, keeping some of the syrup.
Melt the butter with the sugar in a wide pan, add the syrup and the orange zest and juice and simmer.
Stir in the cornflour mixed with water, then add the cherries and warm through.
Off the heat, pour in the brandy and carefully light it with a long match. Let the flames die down.
Spoon over scoops of ice cream.

af.make_ahead: Make the cherry sauce up to 2 days ahead and keep it chilled; reheat, stir in the vanilla and serve over ice cream

steps.text: Drain the cherries, keeping some of the syrup.
Melt the butter with the sugar in a wide pan, add the syrup and the orange zest and juice and simmer.
Stir in the cornflour mixed with water, then add the cherries and warm through.
Off the heat, stir in the vanilla and let the sauce settle for a minute.
Spoon over scoops of ice cream.

dishes.make_ahead: Best made fresh in the mug; stud the lemon slices with cloves up to 1 day ahead

steps.text: Boil water in a kettle.
In each heatproof mug put honey, lemon juice, bourbon and a cinnamon stick.
Top with hot water and stir until the honey dissolves. Stud a lemon slice with cloves and float it on top.

af.n: Mr Hunham's hot honey lemon tea
af.make_ahead: Best made fresh in the mug; stud the lemon slices with cloves up to 1 day ahead

steps.text: Boil water in a kettle.
Steep a tea bag in each heatproof mug of boiling water for 3 minutes, then remove.
Stir in honey, lemon juice, a drop of vanilla and a cinnamon stick until the honey dissolves.
Stud a lemon slice with cloves and float it on top.
